items.title: The dependency-vetting check triggers on workflow action references
body: The security-hygiene.dependency-vetting deterministic trigger keys on package manifests only, so a diff adding googleapis/release-please-action@v5.0.0 — third-party code running with contents:write — showed 'not triggered' and the batch 11 T3 reviewer had to file the missing vetting record by hand.

items.title: Curated starter packs: docs style and code quality that adopters add
body: Owner intent (2026-09-04): adopters should start with a curated default set of rules — docs style and code-quality style in tag-pilot's vein — instead of a near-empty seed. Today template/knowledge/ ships 36 entries that are process-heavy (23 process entries) while quality carries 2 and writing-style 3; no docs-style or language-agnostic code-quality starter content exists.

Shape: curate a default entry set for the quality and writing-style topics (and a docs area if warranted), modeled on the tag-pilot checkout's rules as a READ-ONLY reference (houserules.tag-pilot-is-read-only). Content work, independent of the Tier-2 binary; interacts with HR-053 (a starter set is what a modular rules-only install would seed). Curation choices and any new areas go to the batch spec when gated.
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, mid batch 16.

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.147, meta-spec O13): ships after 2.0.0 as a minor, rescoped to curated starter packs (for example docs style and code quality) that the binary carries and a project adds with pack add; the default stays the knowledge-base pack alone (issue 62), and an added pack is a minor change (D2).

items.title: Narrow check-report-claims' paste-run lint: quote-aware placeholder, $(...)-aware tokenizer
body: Batch 20 T2 fix round 1 review, important findings 3-4: the paste-run lint (HR-071) ships with two measured false-positive vehicles, both disclosed as Limits bullets in crates/houserules/src/report_claims.rs rather than narrowed. (1) The appended-annotation check's subshell exemption only covers a `(...)` wrapping the WHOLE command; a chained `cmd1 && (cmd2)` reads as an appended annotation instead — .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-04-batch-17/task-2-report.json live_run[8] is a real instance the shipped checker flags. (2) The placeholder check ignores quote_mask's state entirely, so a quoted angle-bracket literal that is command DATA (an HTML-comment probe, or a `Co-Authored-By: ... <email>` trailer this repository's own standing no-coauthor rule guarantees will keep generating) misreads as a placeholder — the lint's most frequent false positive at filing time: 5 instances across 4 workspace reports.

The narrowing: (a) a quote-aware placeholder arm in find_placeholder, skipping any span quote_mask already marks as inside a quoted string; (b) a $(...)-aware tokenizer arm in quote_mask, tracking that a same-character quote re-opened inside a `$(...)`/`` `...` `` command substitution starts a fresh, independent quoted region rather than closing the one around the whole substitution (the vehicle report_claims.rs's own Limits section discloses from batch 20 T2's first pass, 2 instances in that same review's own corpus sweep). Deferred per process.no-tech-debt: both are bounded, well-scoped engineering — quote_mask already carries the byte-level state the placeholder check would need to consult, and the $(...) arm needs a small quote-context stack, not a rewrite — not a correctness blocker for HR-071's shipped form, which already discloses both gaps with their measured instances rather than shipping them silently.
Moved out of 2.0.0 to a 2.x minor release by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-21 (design.md 192).
Dropped by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-22 (design.md 212): batch 36 retires the paste-run lint with the inline output it read; the command now comes from the capture header.

items.title: check-backlog gains a --fix arm for a non-round-tripping backlog file

The other five files (schema.json, amendments.json, batches.json, decisions.json, parked.json) have no writer at all, so an adopter who trips this on one of them is told to hand-reproduce serde_json's pretty-printer byte for byte.

Candidate: a `--fix` arm on check-backlog (or a small subcommand) that rewrites the named file through the same `crate::emit::emit` call the check already compares against, so the repair path and the check path stay the same function. Not built in the fix round that filed it: the message-only remedy was the scoped fix; a --fix arm is a larger surface (does it fix every diverging file in one run, or one named file? does it need a --dry-run?) that deserves its own task.
Owner ruling 2026-10-10 (batch-33 Q1, design.md 5.96): not in 2.0.0. It ships after 2.0.0 as a minor release under the 2.0 surface rule (D2).

items.title: check-report-claims: HR-111's multi-file sweep-coverage case
body: Batch 25 T3a fix round 1: check_narrative_sweep_coverage (HR-111) returns early unless a report's files_changed names exactly one file. Measured over the task's own 350-file corpus (t3a-files-changed-reach.py, retained at .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-14-batch-25/): 3 of 350 deliverables carry exactly one files_changed entry (where the check runs), 93 carry more than one, 3 carry an empty files_changed array, and the remaining 251 are review kinds that carry no files_changed field at all -- so the check is inert on 347 of 350 retained deliverables, the common case by a wide margin.

Blocker: this task's corpus run found no reliable signal for WHICH of several changed files a given sweep/enumeration citation is offered as proof for. Comparing a sweep's content against the WHOLE files_changed list once produced a flood of false positives (a narrowly-scoped sweep has no reason to mention a plan file or a schema copy the same task also edited); a two-citation-per-sentence heuristic (the sweep, then a second citation naming the certified file) would have missed the task's own real motivating instance (HR-111's own origin, batch 23 T1: the sentence names only the sweep, relying on the reader knowing which file the task is about). Picking this up needs either a design session to derive a real per-file attribution signal, or a corpus of real multi-file sweep citations large enough to calibrate one against -- this task's own corpus supplied none.
Origin: batch 25 T3a (HR-111); this item schedules the deferred multi-file case rather than leaving it only as a report concern, per process.no-tech-debt.
Rider (batch 25 branch review): see HR-123's split-first note - the same file hosts both items.
Batch 36 split report_claims.rs; the sweep-coverage check lives in crates/houserules/src/report_claims/citations.rs.

items.title: Reports re-open every file:line citation at HEAD; check-report-claims compares the cited line
body: GitHub issue #35 (owner, 2026-09-30). The issue reports from the adopter project orrery, batch 1: process.claims-match-artifacts failed in 7 of 13 tasks, and every failure was drift - a line number, a timestamp, a command string, or a count carried from a draft into the final report. Each failure cost a review round.

Request, two parts. (1) The closing act of the implementer template lists every file-and-line citation in the report after the last edit and re-opens each cited line at HEAD; it copies every command field from the shell history and never retypes a command. (2) check-report-claims resolves each <file>:<line> citation against the tree at HEAD and reports a line whose text differs from the fragment the report quotes.

Triage 2026-10-01: check-report-claims already resolves a citation's file and fails a line number past the end of the file (crates/houserules/src/report_claims.rs); it does not compare the cited line's text with a quoted fragment. Part 2 extends that check. Part 1 changes .claude/agents/implementer.md, so process.evals-rerun applies.

Batch 28 result (2026-10-01): part 1 shipped; part 2 did not. The owner ruled the checker rule heuristic and corpus-gated, with a bar of zero false positives (docs/specs/2026-10-01-batch-28-issue-batch.md, section HR-141; design.md 5.87 directs the batch but does not hold this ruling). The rule as specified (a backticked fragment of the citing sentence must occur in the cited line or range) was measured over the 166 retained deliverables of kind task-report. Hits, classified aged / true / false: as specified 52 = 12 / 2 / 38; fired only on drift evidence (a fragment occurs elsewhere in the cited file) 19 = 9 / 2 / 8; also limited to identifier-shaped fragments 12 = 5 / 2 / 5. At that narrowest trigger the fix-round finding and fix fields give 11 hits = 4 / 2 / 5 and the implemented and self_review fields give 1 hit = 1 / 0 / 0, so a field restriction reaches zero false hits only with zero true hits. Three of the twelve rows at the narrowest trigger are judgment calls, each marked with its alternative class in the classification: one counted true whose alternative is false, one counted false whose alternative is aged, and one counted false whose alternative is true. Taken the other way, they move the false count at that trigger between 3 and 6. The classification counts a hit aged only when the rule passes at a commit the report lists. Under that definition three false hits remain in every variant: a fragment that sits on an adjacent line, fragments that belong to sibling citations in the same sentence, and a fragment that names another job in the cited file. Under the wider definition (a hit is aged whenever the cited file changed after the report), the first of the three counts as aged and the other two remain. Typical false hits: a `grep -c` count such as `read_parity.rs:3` read as a line citation, and a sentence whose backticked token names a command or a neighbor, not code on the cited line. The rule is not wired. Open for a later spec: a trigger with better precision, or an owner ruling that accepts false hits. The module and its tests, unwired, are in the batch-28 workspace on the controller's machine (t5-evidence/wip/); the workspace is not tracked.

Notes for that later spec, from the batch-28 task: (a) a sentence boundary of `.`, `!`, or `?` plus whitespace splits wrongly at `...` inside a backtick span; (b) the classification rests on pre-aggregation commit states, most of them reachable from no ref, so a `git gc` can remove them and the corpus run must be repeated on states that still exist; (c) the tests of the two narrowed variants in the unwired module still expect the finding text of the unnarrowed rule.
Status after batch 28: partial. The template step shipped (with its failure branch) and the range fix of the existing check shipped; the checker rule stays open, as the paragraph above records.
On 2026-10-15 the owner ruled that every open GitHub issue ships in 2.0.0 (design.md 5.98): this item moves to batch 33 (issue 35).

Owner ruling 2026-10-15 (design.md 5.118, meta-spec M12): part 2 ships exact in batch 36 - a citation a claim rests on uses a recorded form a tool fills in at report time (path, line or range, the line's text or hash), and check-report-claims compares it with HEAD; free-prose citations keep the 1.4.0 checks; the unwired batch-28 heuristic module is not wired. Batch 36 holds this item (design.md 5.102).
Back in 2.0.0 by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-21 (design.md 193).

items.title: check-report-claims: a comma-list citation's later line numbers are never checked
body: Found in batch 28 task 5 (HR-141). `check_citation_lines` reads a citation such as `file.rs:23,24,41` for its first number only; the later numbers are not compared with the file's line count. Batch 28 ruled the invariant for a single line and for a range: every line number a citation names fits the file it names. items.title: vacuous-exception-gate looks for the binary under target/debug and panics under CARGO_TARGET_DIR
body: Found by both implementer scenarios of the batch-28 eval rerun. crates/houserules/src/bin/vacuous-exception-gate.rs builds the path of the houserules binary as `<root>/target/debug/<name>`. With `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set to a directory outside the repository, the gate panics on the missing path. Both agents worked around it with a temporary `target` symlink.

Scope for the fix: resolve the binary through the build's own target directory (cargo's `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, or the path of the running gate binary), with a named error when the binary is absent. `mise run lint` runs this gate, so the fix needs a test with the variable set.

items.title: No lint covers a script embedded in a workflow
body: Found in batch 28 task 7. `mise run lint` runs shellcheck over the shell files under tools/, template/tools/, and the commit-msg hooks. A `run:` block of a workflow is a shell script too, and no gate reads it: the seeded install step of template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml (25 lines of bash) and the approve step of .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml are proven only by tests that run them against stubs.

Scope for a spec: extract each `run:` block and pass it to shellcheck in the lint task, or adopt a workflow linter after a dependency vetting. The tests' shared reader (crates/houserules/tests/workflow_reader/) already extracts a step's script.

items.title: Task reports carry generated facts, not prose claims; evidence lives in files the report links
body: Owner (2026-10-09, design.md 5.90): filed as a backlog item, not built in batch 31. The cost analysis of 2026-10-09 measured task reports growing from about 55 KB (batch 2) to 316-635 KB (batches 28 and 30). About half of all 633 review findings across 26 batch workspaces target reports, evidence files, or prose, and the three rules cited most in findings are claim rules (knowledge-base.state-only-the-source 50, process.claims-match-artifacts 35, process.closure-claims-carry-enumeration 21).

Shape for a spec: `houserules` generates the fact fields of a task report (commits, test commands with exit codes, audit rows) instead of the implementer assembling them by hand; command output goes to capture files the report cites by path and hash instead of being pasted verbatim; the free-prose fields shrink to what a reviewer needs. Fewer prose claims leave less for claim rules to check.

Surface: the change edits `.claude/schemas/deliverables.json` and its template copy, a frozen surface (houserules.1-0-surface-is-frozen): a major-version bump and an adopter migration path for existing workspaces.
Back in 2.0.0 by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-21 (design.md 193).

items.title: Evidence by reference: a capture command, inline-output caps, and a checker that reads capture headers
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Issues 3 and 4.

Reports reached 821 KB; one live_run output held 437,126 characters. 25 findings (13 critical) concerned evidence form: retyped commands, a capture in the Windows ANSI code page, re-encoded and re-dated captures. Agents bent captures to pass check-report-claims, and reviewers filed that as fabricated evidence.

Change: `houserules capture --out <file> -- <command...>` runs the command and writes a header (the verbatim command, cwd, ISO start and end times, exit code, HEAD, a dirty flag) above UTF-8 output. Report entries cite the capture path, its hash, and a short excerpt; the deliverables schema caps inline output; check-report-claims verifies headers and hashes instead of parsing shell strings, which retires the cwd, output-filter, and encoding gaps rather than patching each. The audit's checker gaps need the adopter's minimal repros before they are filed separately. The schema cap is a constraint change: 2.0.0 under houserules.1-0-surface-is-frozen, with an adopter migration path. Absorbs HR-057 and HR-158.

body: Owner, 2026-10-21, verbatim: "Make sure that you rewrite the readme when we publish v2. Users must know at a glance when and why houserules is the right solution for them and they must know that houserules can be the central layer that keeps their ai-native coding consistent instead of diverging into whatever agents deem correct in the moment with their limited knowledge of a session. Adhere to the best-practices of README writing that you have once researched and make sure to research beforehand, what makes houserules unique and strong against other solutions and make those advantages clear."

Scope: (1) Research first, at spec time, with sources recorded in the batch workspace: current README practice (re-checked against the batch-26 research of design.md 84 and writing-style.readme-is-an-adopter-funnel), and what makes houserules unique and strong against the other solutions that adopters weigh (for example per-harness rule files such as AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules, and Copilot instructions; rule-sync tools; spec-driven toolkits such as OpenSpec and Spec Kit; agent memory banks); each claimed advantage is verified against the tree and the sources, never assumed. (3) The rest follows the adopter funnel: value, install, runnable usage, then depth; no process history, no claims that rot with releases. (4) The README makes clear that houserules integrates cleanly with those other solutions, a strength of 2.0 in its own right: it renders into the harnesses' own rule files, reads work items through the adopter's tracker, and works under OpenSpec and other workflows; each integration claim is shown by a run, not asserted. items.title: Organize the knowledge by Diátaxis and generate human-readable documentation from it
body: Owner request 2026-10-23, verbatim: "Backlog item for 2.x: i want the knowledge to be organized according to the Diátaxis pattern. We need to brainstorm how we can add a generator into houserules such that human-readable documentation can be generated from the knowledge base."
